title: Metric spike sleuthing notebook
content:
Goal: quick, messy debug notes for the partial metrics spike + downstream metric drop that started ~2024-10-28 03:42 UTC. This is my personal notebook: steps I ran, commands, raw snippets and hypotheses. Not polished; keep it here until I move a cleaned playbook to Confluence.

Symptoms observed:
- sudden 6x ingest rate reported by proxy_metrics.ingest_requests (rolling 1m) for a 4 minute window beginning 2024-10-28 03:42:11 UTC.
- downstream aggregated service metrics (frontend-requests.success_rate) briefly dipped ~3 percentage points starting 03:43:xx.
- traces: sampling count unchanged, but many traces missing traceparent header in the proxy layer for a subset of requests.
- logs: a burst of WARNs from ingest-proxy: "kv-cache-miss-path:missing_key" and repeated "parsePayload: truncated" entries.

Commands run (order-ish):
1) tail recent proxy logs locally (k8s):
   kubectl -n observability logs deploy/ingest-proxy --since=15m | grep -E "parsePayload|missing_key|traceparent" -n | tail -n 200
   -> saw ~780 parsePayload: truncated entries between 03:42:07-03:46:12.

2) grep raw request IDs and try replay one sample:
   kubectl -n observability logs deploy/ingest-proxy | jq -r 'select(.msg|test("parsePayload")) | .request_id' | head -n 10
   curl -v -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "X-Request-ID: <sample>" --data-binary @sample-bad-payload.json https://ingest.redwood.internal/v1/receive
   -> 400 Bad Request, body: {"error":"payload_truncated","code":422}.

3) confirm client-side retry storms? looked at api-gateway: request_rate for same request_id prefixes spiked but origin IPs were distributed (not single client).

4) check trace sampling headers around spikes:
   kubectl -n observability logs deploy/api-gateway | grep traceparent | sed -n '1,200p'
   -> many ingress lines without traceparent; some with malformed traceparent (too short).

5) pulled raw ingress payloads from S3 archive for the window: s3://redwood-raw/ingest/2024/10/28/03/*.gz
   zcat | jq -r '.headers|{traceparent: .traceparent, content_length: .Content-Length, reqid: .X-Request-ID}' | head -n 50
   -> several entries had Content-Length > actual body length (mismatch).

Quick error snippets (copied directly):
- ingest-proxy: "WARN parsePayload: truncated (expected 16384, got 12034) request_id=r-8d3f..."
- api-gateway: "WARN trace-parse: invalid traceparent len=20 header='00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e473b-0000000000000000-01'"
- kv-store: "ERROR write-failed: context deadline exceeded (30s) key=route-cache:user-xyz"

Hypotheses (brainstorm):
- H1: Upstream client or proxy is misreporting Content-Length leading to truncated-reads in ingest-proxy which then rejects and triggers client retries. The retry bursts amplify ingest_requests metric temporarily.
- H2: A recent change in api-gateway parsing code (PR #: https://github.com/redwood-inference/api-gateway/pull/543) introduced a lax traceparent acceptor that strips or mangles headers for certain keep-alive chunked requests. Missing traceparent means traces break, and the failure path scrubs some metrics consumers.
- H3: Intermittent network blips between ingest-proxy and KV cache cause write timeouts. Requests are re-sent, but some partial writes make downstream metrics report failures.
- H4: A bad batch of client payloads (e.g., older SDK version) started to be routed to the new proxy instance due to a canary routing rule; the instance has a slightly different max-body config and drops trailing bytes.

Local reproduction attempts:
- Created sample payload and used `tcpdump` to capture actual bytes on proxy pod:
  kubectl exec -n observability deploy/ingest-proxy -- tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w /tmp/cap.pcap port 443 &
  (replay sample)
  kubectl cp ingest-proxy:/tmp/cap.pcap ./cap.pcap && wireshark -> saw that client sent chunked transfer-encoding but Content-Length header present (contradiction) which confused proxy reader.

- Replayed with curl using chunked body, server responded 400 when both chunked and Content-Length present.

Instrumented quick patch locally (hotfix) to log both Transfer-Encoding and Content-Length at debug and to refuse requests with both headers present (instead of attempting to read Content-Length). Deployed to staging: ingress-acceptance tests showed no regressions; staging loadtest with old-sdk client produced the same truncated behavior when both headers were present.

Observability gaps found while debugging:
- No metric for "requests_with_both_content_length_and_chunked". Small audit metric would have flagged fast.
- Trace header parsing failures are WARN-only and not emitted as a metric.
- S3 raw archive ingestion pipeline strips some headers which would be helpful for correlating.

Immediate mitigation options (fast -> slower):
- short term: edge rule to drop Content-Length if Transfer-Encoding: chunked present (NGINX/ALB rewrite) at lb layer for a few hours. Lower risk to clients but might hide real client bug.
- medium: force-proxy-drop for requests with contradictory headers and emit metric + alert - implement hotfix (already instrumented debug logs) and roll to prod canary.
- long: add strict schema validation on client SDK (and deprecate old SDK versions) + add ingestion-side schema metric and proper backpressure handling.

Next steps I'm planning (todo):
- [ ] Open a short-lived alert: METRIC spike + parsePayloadTruncated > 5/min -> page on-call and annotate incident timeline (JIRA-INGEST-982).
- [ ] Add metric and dashboard tile for contradictory header combos. (small infra change).
- [ ] Deploy canary hotfix that returns 422 and increments new metric so we can quantify scope.
- [ ] Coordinate with SDK owners: share sample bad payload and ask for version + user-agent.
- [ ] If mitigations insufficient, put an LB rewrite rule to coerce headers for known user agents.

Notes to self (sparse):
- Watch for correlation between KV-store timeouts and parsePayload: truncated. Could be separate but worth verifying (check pod restarts, OOM).
- Compare proxy version on node pool q4-a vs q4-b (are we running different images?).
- Remember to include sample pcap and sample-bad-payload.json in Confluence incident artifact repo.

Rough timeline (local timeline build):
- 03:41:55 initial minor increase in requests (5-10% over baseline).
- 03:42:11 parsePayload truncated first observed.
- 03:43:00 retries escalate, ingest_requests metric peaks at 6x baseline.
- 03:44:20 downstream success_rate drops ~3 pts.
- 03:46:55 partial recovery as new LB route evens traffic.

If you pick this up: look at nodepool q4-b autoscaler events around 03:40-03:50 (I saw some scale up events but not sure if correlated). Also check whether any deploys to api-gateway or ingest-proxy happened 24–48h before.

Raw artifacts saved locally: ./artifacts/cap.pcap, ./artifacts/sample-bad-payload.json, ./artifacts/proxy-logs-03-42-03-47.gz

-- Asha Khatri (personal scratchpad)
